title: Mount jog arrows are silently dead while the mount is parked
what_happened: While the mount reported Parked, clicking the E arrow produced no motion, no toast and no log entry at all (the first 'Pulse guiding' line in the native log appears only after Unpark). The pad's only disabled affordance is a slightly dimmer icon colour, which is not distinguishable from the enabled state on this dark theme.
expected: Either disable the pad visibly (dim the whole pad / show a 'Mount is parked' tooltip or inline hint), or accept the press and surface 'Mount is parked - unpark first'.
repro: Dashboard with Mount Control widget, mount Parked -> click any arrow. Compare /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-wizards-28.png (parked) with r-wizards-29.png (unparked): the arrow pad renders identically.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-wizards-28.png vs -29.png; app.log has no 'Pulse guiding' line for the parked click at 14:36.
proposed_fix: Wrap the pad in an Opacity/overlay when disabled and set the Tooltip message to the reason ('Mount is parked').
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. With the sim mount Parked, clicking E then N appended ZERO new lines to /tmp/ns-audit/v2-wizards/app.log (line count unchanged at 97), no snackbar/alert appeared in the a11y tree, RA stayed 00:00:00. After Unpark the identical click immediately logged 'Pulse guiding ... east', so the pad really was inert only because of the parked gate. Cited lines are exact: mount_control_card.dart:175 is 'isEnabled: isConnected && !mountState.isParked,' and :413 is 'onTap: isEnabled ? onPressed : null,' (InkWell opens at :412). The disabled-affordance claim holds too: _DirectionalButton keeps Material(color: colors.surfaceAlt) in both states and changes only the Icon colour (textPrimary -> textMuted, :419-421).

title: Dashboard Widgets picker lists two different widgets both called "Guiding"
what_happened: The Dashboard Widgets dialog contains two separate rows named "Guiding": one described 'RMS error and guiding graph' (checked by default) and, ~10 rows later, another described 'RMS and guiding graph' (unchecked). There is also a 'Weather & Safety' and a plain 'Weather', and an 'Equipment Telemetry' and a plain 'Equipment'. A user cannot tell which one they are toggling.
expected: Every row in the picker has a unique, distinguishable name, or the legacy/duplicate entries are removed.
repro: Dashboard -> Edit Dashboard -> Widgets -> scroll the list.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-wizards-17.png (Guiding - 'RMS error and guiding graph', checked) and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-wizards-20.png (Guiding - 'RMS and guiding graph', unchecked) in the same dialog.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/dashboard/widgets/widget_picker_dialog.dart and the widget registry that feeds it
proposed_fix: De-duplicate the registry (the second set looks like the pre-cockpit widget ids) or rename them so the distinction is explicit.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live. Dashboard -> Edit Dashboard -> Widgets, scrolling the list, the a11y tree reports 'check box: Guiding' twice in the SAME dialog: once in the cockpit block (between 'Equipment Telemetry' and 'Weather & Safety') and again ~14 rows later in the legacy block (between 'Sequence Status' and 'Equipment'). The dialog also lists 'Weather & Safety' and 'Weather', and 'Equipment Telemetry' and 'Equipment'. Source matches: widget_picker_dialog.dart:71-101 iterates the whole dashboardWidgetRegistry rendering definition.title verbatim; dashboard_widget_registry.dart:162-169 is id cockpitGuiding title 'Guiding' subtitle 'RMS error and guiding graph' and :337-344 is id guiding title 'Guiding' subtitle 'RMS and guiding graph' - both subtitles quoted in the finding are verbatim correct. 'where' is accurate.

title: Glance mode toggle on the Dashboard changes nothing on the Dashboard
what_happened: The eye icon in the dashboard command bar is the Glance mode toggle ('bumps the dashboard's secondary-status type up so the run can be read from across the room'). Toggling it on tints the button and the tooltip flips to 'Glance mode: on', but a pixel diff of the whole dashboard content area (1000x700 px) between on and off differs in only a 4x12 px sliver at the panel edge - 0.005% of pixels. No text on the dashboard gets larger.
expected: Either the dashboard's status readouts (target, exposure countdown, HFR, RMS, frame counts) scale up when glance mode is on, or the toggle does not live on the dashboard.
repro: Dashboard -> click the eye icon in the command bar (right of the Local chip) -> click it again. Compare /tmp/ns-audit/shots/glance-on.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/glance-off.png.
evidence: PIL diff of glance-on.png vs glance-off.png: bbox (996,39,1000,51), 0.0047% of pixels differ by >10. Source: SkotiqTypography.glanceStyle has exactly two callers repo-wide, both in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/widgets/run_dashboard/ (session_warnings_panel.dart:142, filter_integration_panel.dart:178) - neither is on the Dashboard screen.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/dashboard/widgets/glance_mode_toggle.dart (control) vs the two glanceStyle consumers in the sequencer run dashboard
location_wrong: The finding's supporting claim that neither glanceStyle consumer 'is on the Dashboard screen' is FALSE. dashboard_widget_registry.dart registers BOTH as dashboard tiles: cockpitFilterIntegration -> RunDashboardFilterIntegration (registry ~143-151 / 471-477) and cockpitSessionWarnings -> RunDashboardSessionWarningsPanel (~180-187 / 503-509). They ARE on the Dashboard; they simply render nothing outside an active run. Correct 'where' is glance_mode_toggle.dart plus the fact that only those two run-scoped panels opt in, not the always-visible status readouts.
proposed_fix: Apply SkotiqTypography.glanceStyle to the dashboard command-bar metrics, the Now Imaging / target strip and the exposure countdown, or move the toggle to the sequencer run dashboard where its two consumers actually live.
verdict_reasoning: Symptom reproduced. Dashboard with sim camera + mount connected (cockpit awake, Filter Integration / Session Warnings / Mount Control enabled). Full-res captures before and after clicking the eye toggle; a11y tree confirms the flip ('Glance mode [off]' -> '[ON]'). Pixel diff shows changes ONLY in the command bar (toggle chip + ticking clock, y 228-260) and in the right rail at x 1520-1677 - and a control diff of two captures 5 s apart in the SAME glance state shows the identical right-rail drift (live heartbeat events / sensor temp). No text changed size anywhere. Source explains it: session_warnings_panel.dart returns SizedBox.shrink() with no warnings and filter_integration_panel.dart emits its glanceStyle text only per configured filter, so with no run nothing glance-styled is on screen, and the readouts the tooltip implies (Temp/Focus/HFR/RMS/target) never call glanceStyle. Downgraded to P3: misleading affordance, not data or safety, and it does have a narrow real effect during a run.

title: All-Sky reticle labels collide: the error marker, the az/alt caption and the "Dn" compass label are drawn on top of each other
what_happened: In All-Sky mode with a result showing, the red error marker sits underneath the caption 'Az -351.4\" Alt -1765.4\"' (the dot bisects the '-351.4' text), and that caption in turn overlaps the 'Dn' axis label of the compass rose. Three separate elements occupy the same ~30 px band.
expected: The marker must draw above/around the labels, and the numeric caption must be placed outside the reticle (or the reticle padded) so the compass labels stay legible.
repro: Run TPPA to completion, then switch the segmented control to All-Sky. Right rail.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-125.png (close-up of the reticle: '1800.0\"' then 'Az -35[dot]4\"  Alt -1765.4\"' overlapping 'Dn').
proposed_fix: Paint the marker last, and lay the numeric caption below the reticle box rather than inside it.
verdict_reasoning: Confirmed by exact geometry in the cited file (all_sky_target_reticle.dart is the right file). In one SizedBox(size,size) Stack: (1) the caption Column is 'Positioned(bottom: 8, left: 0, right: 0)' (:92-95) with a 22px total-error Text over an 11px 'Az ... Alt ...' Text (:112-125), so the az/alt line sits at roughly y = size-22 .. size-8, centred. (2) _drawCardinal(bottomCenter) (:222, :351-354) puts 'Dn' at center.dy + radius + padding with radius = min(w,h)/2 - 16, padding 4, i.e. top edge at y = size-12 on the same x - inside the caption band, running a pixel past the bottom edge. (3) the marker dot (:304-307, r=6) is clamped to maxRadius, so an altitude-dominated error like Alt -1765.4" of a 1800" total pins it to bottom-centre at y = size-16, the same band; the caption is a later Stack child so it paints OVER the dot, matching 'the dot bisects the -351.4 text'. Three elements in one ~30px band by construction, no guard. Not driven live: an All-Sky result needs a plate solve and the scratch profile reports 'No plate solver is configured', so this is verified from layout arithmetic rather than a screenshot.

title: Collaborative Sky dialogs render inside an empty full-height slab
what_happened: 'Connect to a hub', 'Start co-imaging session' and 'Share your co-imaging subs' all draw their content card inside a taller, lighter-toned panel that runs from y=20 to y=700 of the 720 px window - roughly 300 px of empty surface above the dialog title and 150 px below its buttons. It reads as a rendering fault rather than a scrim: the slab is a distinct, lighter colour than the dimmed page behind it and has hard vertical edges at the dialog's width.
expected: The dialog surface should wrap its content.
repro: Plan Tonight -> Discover -> Collaborate -> Connect to a hub.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-169.png, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-174.png, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-175.png - in each, the light slab spans x 433-847 for the full window height while the dialog card occupies only the middle third.
location_wrong: Not 'collaborative_sky/ dialog scaffolding'. The defect is a nested-dialog mismatch between a shared helper and three sheet bodies, one of which lives outside that directory. showAdaptiveModal's desktop branch (packages/skotiq_ui/lib/src/layout/adaptive_modal.dart:102-127) already wraps the body in a Material Dialog painted colors.surface, sized 'SizedBox(width: size.width, height: size.height)' where AdaptiveDialogConstraints.dialogSize returns height: NULL when designHeight is omitted (adaptive_dialog_constraints.dart:46-48). The three offending bodies then return a SECOND dialog: constellation_sign_in_sheet.dart:53, coimaging_create_sheet.dart:155, mosaic_contribute_sheet.dart:196. Fix belongs at those three call sites (or in showAdaptiveModal).
proposed_fix: Give the dialog container mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min / drop the background from the outer constrained box.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. Plan Tonight -> Discover -> Collaborate -> 'Connect to a hub': a lighter slab spans x 433-847 from y~20 to y~700 of the 720 px window while the dialog card occupies only y 170-549 - about 150 px of empty surface above the title and 150 px below the buttons (the finding's 'roughly 300 px above' overstates it; everything else matches). Pixel sampling proves it is a real surface, not the scrim: slab (17,20,24), dimmed page either side (5,6,7), dialog card (24,28,34). Isolating control: 'Name a region' (your_sky/widgets/name_region_sheet.dart:26) also calls showAdaptiveModal WITHOUT designHeight but does not return a SkotiqDialog, and renders correctly wrapped (y 222-497) - so the slab comes from the nested SkotiqDialog, not showAdaptiveModal alone. Exactly the three dialogs the finding named are exactly the three showAdaptiveModal bodies that return SkotiqDialog.

title: The same mosaic is described as "3x2 grid" on one screen and "2x3 grid" on the other
what_happened: A project stored as rows=2, cols=3 is rendered '3x2 grid - 6 panels' by the Mosaic projects list and the project header, and '2x3 grid' by the Collaborative mosaics card for the very same mosaic. Nothing on either screen says whether the first number is columns or rows.
expected: One convention, stated once (e.g. '3 wide x 2 high').
repro: Publish a mosaic, then compare the project header with the Collaborate list entry.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-193.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-194.png ('3x2 grid') vs /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-201.png ('2x3 grid'). DB: rows=2, cols=3.
proposed_fix: A single shared formatter, e.g. '${cols} x ${rows} panels (w x h)'.
verdict_reasoning: Confirmed by exact source inspection; the two formatters really do transpose. mosaic_project_screen.dart:470 emits '${project.cols}x${project.rows} grid' and mosaic_projects_list_screen.dart:152 emits the same cols-first string, while collaborative_sky/widgets/collab_mosaic_card.dart:86 emits '${mosaic.rows}x${mosaic.cols} grid' (with a U+00D7 sign) - rows first. A project stored rows=2, cols=3 therefore renders '3x2 grid' on both mosaic screens and '2x3 grid' on the Collaborate card, and neither string says which axis is which. The finding's 'where' is right in substance; the precise collaborative-side line is collab_mosaic_card.dart:86, not the screen file. Not driven end-to-end (needs a hub), but these are unconditional literals with no branch that could make them agree.

title: The mosaic project screen's back breadcrumb always says "Mosaic projects" even when it returns somewhere else
what_happened: I reached /mosaic/:id from the Collaborative Sky mosaic detail (via 'Join mosaic'), not from the Mosaic projects list. The header breadcrumb still read '< Mosaic projects'. Pressing it returned me to the Collaborative Sky mosaic detail page, not to the mosaic projects list.
expected: Either label the control generically ('Back') or label it with the actual previous route.
repro: Collaborate -> tap a mosaic -> Join mosaic -> press the '< Mosaic projects' breadcrumb.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-203.png ('< Mosaic projects' visible on the project screen reached from Collaborate) and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-207.png (what it actually returns to: the Collaborative mosaic detail).
proposed_fix: Use a plain back affordance, or pass the origin label through the route extra.
verdict_reasoning: Confirmed by source. mosaic_project_screen.dart:426-430 renders a bare 'Mosaic projects' string literal beside the back IconButton - no parameter, provider or route inspection feeds it. The handler _leave (:439-446) is 'if (navigator.canPop()) { navigator.pop(); return; } context.go('/mosaic');' - it pops to whatever is underneath and only falls back to the projects list on an empty stack. The claimed entry path is real: collab_mosaic_detail_screen.dart:386-390 does 'await navigator.push(MaterialPageRoute(builder: (_) => MosaicProjectScreen(projectId: projectId)))' after Join mosaic, so the route underneath is the Collaborative-Sky mosaic detail and the control labelled 'Mosaic projects' returns there. 'where' is accurate.
